newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt yields lower following offshore.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt yields lower following offshore.

text.p: Swedish bond yields fell on Tuesday morning in line with lower yields in Germany.
Nine year bond yields fell by five basis points to 7.13 percent and the six month T-bill rate climbed by one basis point to 4.62 percent.
The crown weakened slightly to 4.3010 against the mark compared to 4.2950 late Monday.
As expected Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, kept its repo rate at 4.95 percent at its weekly tender.
But dealers said there was still some uncertainty in the market about the meaning of a Riksbank statement last week.
Deputy governor Lars Heikensten said the bank did not necessarily have to follow a certain pattern with its repo rate in the future.

Some analysts interpreted this as a possible cue for a more relaxed policy while others believed the Riksbank would soon start to lower the pace in the repo rate cuts which have been coming every two weeks since the start of the year.
The market was now focusing on the release at 1230 GMT on Wednesday of the U.S.'s consumer price index for September.
